history.dynasty: Unknown (natural cave shrine; no documented builder)
history.period: Date of construction unknown; mythological (Ramayana) associations
history.summary: Sita Gufaa is a small natural cave shrine in Panchavati, Nashik, believed in Hindu tradition to be where Sita stayed and worshipped an ancient Shivlinga during the 14-year exile of Rama, and the spot from where Ravana abducted her. The cave is reached through a very narrow staircase/low entrance (visitors must crouch), and inside are idols of Rama, Sita and Lakshmana alongside the old Shivlinga. Outside stands a grove of five very old banyan trees that give Panchavati ('garden of five banyans') its name; the entire Aranya Kanda of the Ramayana is set in this area, with Kalaram Temple and Ramkund on the Godavari within walking distance. No historical construction date or dynasty is documented for the cave in web sources; it is a site of living worship, not an ASI-style monument.

name: Sita Gufaa (Sita Cave) Temple
town_description: Nashik is an ancient city on the banks of the Godavari in northwest Maharashtra, one of the four cities that host the Kumbh Mela (the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha). It is deeply tied to the Ramayana: the Panchavati area, where this cave stands, is traditionally where Rama, Sita and Lakshmana lived during exile, and nearby Trimbakeshwar hosts one of the twelve Jyotirlingas. Today it is a major pilgrimage and wine-industry centre with good road and rail links to Mumbai.

travel.railway: Nashik Road Railway Station, approx. 11 km (per indulgexpress) (verify).
travel.road: ~2.7-3 km from Nashik Central Bus Station; auto-rickshaws and city buses serve Panchavati; parking scarce, use Ram Kund area.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (12-28 degC); early mornings 6:30-8:30 AM to avoid crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 9:00 PM daily (some sources say 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM - CONFLICT (verify)). No entry fee; photography restricted inside; narrow entrance unsuitable for the elderly or mobility-impaired.
